Pakistan posted 134 in their second innings, shifting match momentum decisively through crucial partnerships.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Headingley commenced with high tactical intensity as Pakistan posted 174/10 (48.1 ov) in their opening innings. In response, England countered with 363/10 (106.2 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 10 Wickets for 114 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, James Anderson delivered a masterclass for England (5 Runs & 5 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (England 61%) and allowing England to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Pakistan faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. England's bowling unit, bolstered by Stuart Broad (2 Runs & 6 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing England won by innings & 55 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: England's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Pakistan produced fighting phases, England won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
